description: MCP server exposing WinDbg/DbgEng (live user-mode, kernel, crash dumps, TTD) to AI agents over stdio
notes: Basic live/crash-dump debugging works out of the box with the System32 engine.
For TTD replay and crash-dump !analyze, bundle the WinDbg engine DLLs next to the binary.
If WinDbg (Microsoft.WinDbg) is installed from the Store, post_install copies them automatically.
Disconnect the MCP server from any connected client before updating (scoop update windbg-mcp).
A connected client holds the exe open, since the server re-executes its own image to spawn engine workers.
post_install: # 64-bit engine payload: loose DLLs beside windbg-mcp.exe, plus triage/ttd/winext subdirs.
# kdexts.dll (!drvobj/!devobj/!irp for the driver tools) lives in winxp; copy just that file.
# 32-bit engine payload: for 32-bit .NET (WoW64) targets, which the bundled x86\windbg-mcp.exe worker drives.
# Must live in the x86 subdir next to the x86 worker, never beside the x64 exe.
Write-Host 'WinDbg engine bundled for TTD replay, !analyze, kernel and 32-bit .NET debugging support.' -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host 'WinDbg (Microsoft.WinDbg) not found. Basic debugging works, but TTD replay' -ForegroundColor Yellow
Write-Host 'and !analyze require the WinDbg engine. See: scoop info windbg-mcp' -ForegroundColor Yellow
